mainTopic: רבי יוסי's view on the three-month wait and on engagement during mourning, and a new משנה on יבום with several widows
overview: The גמרא continues examining רבי יוסי's opinion about the three-month wait before a woman remarries (הבחנה). First it asks whether he rejects the wait entirely. It answers either that he does, or that he only lets women who were engaged and then divorced marry right away. That second answer makes him sound like רבי יהודה, so the גמרא finds a difference: רבי יוסי forbids a fully married woman to become engaged within three months. A ברייתא seems to contradict this, so רבא rewords the ברייתא. That rewording is in turn attacked, because a woman widowed from engagement does not mourn. The גמרא then defends רבי יוסי against the earlier קל וחומר about mourning before תשעה באב. It first suggests the question is a מחלוקת תנאים. When רב אשי weakens the proof for that, he answers that a widow's new, private mourning is stricter than the old, public mourning for the חורבן. Finally, a new משנה begins about יבום: one brother may do יבום with several widows, and יבום or חליצה with one wife releases her צרה.

steps.title: Does רבי יוסי reject the waiting rule completely?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוסי really does not hold of the three-month wait for הבחנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't רבי יוסי hold that a woman must wait in order to tell the fathers apart?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new wording it just gave to רבי יוסי's opinion. Under that wording, he seems never to require the three-month wait.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's main rule is that a woman waits three months before remarrying, so that if she is pregnant we know whose child it is. If רבי יוסי lets every woman marry right away, he seems to drop that rule entirely, and that is surprising.

keyTerms.meaning: to tell apart: the reason for the three-month wait, so we know which husband is the father
he does not hold of it

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yosei not hold of waiting to tell apart?
phrases.notes: He means waiting three months, so that if she is pregnant we know which husband is the father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new wording of רבי יוסי from the previous section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reworked wording of רבי יוסי in the משנה (all women may marry right away).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That wording seems to remove the basic rule of הבחנה, which everyone in the משנה appears to accept.

steps.title: Yes, רבי יוסי does not hold of it
steps.stepSummary: First answer: indeed, רבי יוסי does not accept the three-month wait.
steps.simpleTranslation: He really does not hold of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא simply accepts the challenge: רבי יוסי does not require the wait for הבחנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing has to be explained away. The גמרא says רבי יוסי simply has his own view and does not accept the decree. The only waiting he requires is a widow's mourning period.

phrases.english: He does not hold of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 1 by accepting what it suggested.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It would be strange for רבי יוסי to reject הבחנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He really does reject it; that is his own opinion.

steps.title: He does hold of the wait, but the wording changes
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: רבי יוסי does accept הבחנה, and his words should be read as allowing only women who were engaged and then divorced to marry right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you could say: he really does hold of it. Read רבי יוסי's words as: all women who were only engaged and then divorced may marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way out. רבי יוסי does keep the waiting rule, and we change his words so that only engaged-and-divorced women skip it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who was only engaged never lived with her husband, so there is no doubt about who the father would be. Under this reading, רבי יוסי still requires a fully married woman to wait.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you wish, say: introduces a second answer
women who were only engaged (betrothed), not yet fully married

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two stages apart. אֵרוּסִין (engagement/betrothal) is the first stage, and נִשּׂוּאִין (full marriage) is the second stage, when the couple lives together. The whole discussion depends on this difference.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
actually, he does hold of it,
and say that Rabbi Yosei says:
all women who were betrothed and divorced may be married.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 1, different from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי lets every woman marry right away, so he rejects הבחנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only women who were engaged and then divorced may marry right away. A fully married woman still waits.

steps.title: Then רבי יוסי is the same as רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוסי only lets engaged-and-divorced women marry, his view seems identical to רבי יהודה's.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, that is just רבי יהודה's opinion!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second answer. The new reading makes רבי יוסי say the same thing as רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה already says that women who were only engaged may marry. Two תנאים are not listed as if they disagree when they say the same thing.

phrases.english: If so, this is the same as Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in step 3, that engaged-and-divorced women may marry.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading gives רבי יוסי the same view as רבי יהודה, so there would be no reason to state it as a separate opinion.

steps.title: The difference: a married woman becoming engaged
steps.stepSummary: They differ about a woman who was fully married and now wants to become engaged. רבי יהודה allows it, and רבי יוסי forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: a woman who was married and wants to become engaged. רבי יהודה says she may become engaged. רבי יוסי says she may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by finding a practical case where the two תנאים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that a woman who was only engaged may marry right away. They differ about a woman who was fully married. רבי יהודה lets her become engaged within the three months, but רבי יוסי makes her wait even for the engagement.

keyTerms.meaning: there is a difference between them
a woman who was fully married

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: a married woman becoming betrothed.
phrases.notes: This is a woman who was fully married to her first husband and now wants to get engaged within the three months.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds:
a married woman is permitted to be betrothed.
And Rabbi Yosei holds:
a married woman is forbidden to be betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by pointing to a case where the two views differ.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה say exactly the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ about a married woman becoming engaged within three months. רבי יהודה permits it and רבי יוסי forbids it.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the second answer, רבי יוסי is stricter than רבי יהודה: a woman who was fully married may not even become engaged during the three months.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יוסי allows engagement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 5 with a ברייתא in which רבי יוסי lets all women become engaged right away, except a widow during her thirty days of mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי really hold that a married woman may not become engaged? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי says all women may become engaged, except a widow, because of her mourning. How long is her mourning? Thirty days. And none of them may marry until three months have passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict what it just said about רבי יוסי. Steps 7 to 9 work through this challenge, and רבא answers it in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said רבי יוסי forbids a married woman to become engaged within three months. In this ברייתא, he allows every woman to become engaged right away, and the only exception is a widow, because of mourning, not הבחנה. He requires the three-month wait only for the actual marriage.
steps.confusionAlert: The widow's thirty days come from mourning, not from הבחנה. Those are two different reasons for waiting.

phrases.aramaic: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי נְשׂוּאָה אֲסוּרָה לֵיאָרֵס?
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yosei hold that a married woman is forbidden to be betrothed?
But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
all women may be betrothed,
phrases.notes: "All women" includes a woman who was fully married. That is exactly what step 5 said he forbids.

phrases.english: except for the widow, because of the mourning,
and how long is her mourning? Thirty days.
And none of them may be married
until they have had three months.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי נְשׂוּאָה אֲסוּרָה לֵיאָרֵס וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the difference proposed in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 5 that רבי יוסי forbids a married woman to become engaged within three months.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי allowing all women to become engaged right away. The only exception is a widow, because of mourning, so a married woman is clearly allowed.

steps.title: The opening words of the ברייתא are not a real problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the challenge really is. If it comes from the opening words 'all women may become engaged,' we can reread them just as we reread the משנה: they mean engaged-then-divorced women may marry.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difficulty here? If it is because the ברייתא says 'רבי יוסי says: all women may become engaged,' is the ברייתא any stronger than our משנה? We already explained the משנה as 'engaged women who were divorced may marry.' Here too, read it as 'all engaged divorced women may marry.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask which part of the ברייתא is causing trouble. It shows that the first line is not a real problem, which sets up the real challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3 we already reread the משנה's words 'all women may become engaged' to mean 'engaged-and-divorced women may marry.' The ברייתא uses the same words, so the same rereading works for it too. That is why its opening line cannot knock down step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difficulty? (asking what exactly the challenge is)
We explained it as (we set the text in a certain case)
Women who were only engaged and then divorced

phrases.english: This — what is the difficulty?
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא quoted in step 6. Why does it really challenge us?

phrases.english: If you say it is because it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים יִתְאָרְסוּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: all women may become engaged
is it any stronger than our משנה,
which we explained as: engaged women who were divorced may marry?
Here too, read it as:
all engaged women who were divorced may marry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows down the challenge of step 6 by showing that its first line can be answered.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only one possible basis for the challenge, the opening words of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The opening words can be reread exactly like the משנה's identical words were reread in step 3.

steps.title: The real problem comes from the end of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: 'none of them may marry until three months.' This suggests that only marrying is forbidden and becoming engaged is allowed. That contradicts step 5, which said רבי יוסי forbids a married woman from getting engaged.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the problem is from the end of the ברייתא, which teaches: 'And none of them may marry until they have waited three months.' This means only marrying is not allowed, but becoming engaged is fine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the true challenge. The last line of the ברייתא suggests that רבי יוסי lets married women become engaged right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue about a fully married woman who wants to become engaged, and that רבי יוסי forbids it. The ברייתא's last line limits the three-month wait to marrying, so engagement is permitted. That would leave רבי יוסי agreeing with רבי יהודה again.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of a teaching

phrases.english: Rather, the problem is from the end, which teaches:
and none of them may marry
until they have waited three months.
So it is only marrying that is not allowed,
but becoming engaged is fine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 7 shows that the opening line is not the problem, this step finds the real problem in the end of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 5's claim that רבי יוסי forbids a fully married woman from becoming engaged within three months.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says only marrying requires three months, which implies engagement is allowed right away.

steps.title: רבא rewords רבי יוסי's statement
steps.stepSummary: רבא fixes the wording: engaged-and-divorced women may marry right away, except a widow, who must wait her thirty days of mourning. Fully married women may not even become engaged until three months.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Fix the text and say it like this: רבי יוסי says, all engaged women who were divorced may marry, except a widow, because of mourning. How long is her mourning? Thirty days. And women who were fully married may not become engaged until they have waited three months.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by rereading the whole ברייתא. In his version, the three-month rule for married women covers even becoming engaged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא keeps the idea that רבי יוסי argues with רבי יהודה about married women becoming engaged. In his version the last line says 'may not become engaged' instead of 'may not marry.' The widow exception now refers to a woman widowed from engagement, who must wait thirty days of mourning.

keyTerms.meaning: Fix the wording and say it like this

phrases.english: Rava said:
Fix it and say it like this:
Rabbi Yosei says:
all engaged women who were divorced may marry,
except the widow, because of mourning.
phrases.notes: In רבא's version, this widow is one whose husband died while they were only engaged.

phrases.english: And how long is her mourning?
Thirty days.
And women who were fully married may not become engaged
until they have waited three months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by rewording the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that married women may become engaged right away and only marrying is delayed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read correctly, married women may not even become engaged for three months, so step 5 stands. The widow exception is about an engaged widow and her thirty days.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two groups. 'Engaged divorced women' may MARRY right away, but 'married women' may not even become ENGAGED for three months.

steps.title: A woman widowed from engagement does not mourn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: does a widow from engagement mourn at all? A ברייתא of רבי חייא בר אמי teaches that engaged partners do not mourn each other, so רבא's widow exception does not fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does a widow from engagement have mourning? Didn't רבי חייא בר אמי teach: If his engaged wife died, he is not an אונן and does not become impure for her. And likewise, if he died, she is not an אוננת and does not become impure for him. If she dies, he does not inherit her. If he dies, she collects her כתובה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's rewording. It uses a ברייתא showing that a woman whose engaged husband died has no mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's version says an engaged widow must wait thirty days of mourning. רבי חייא בר אמי's ברייתא teaches that between engaged partners there is no mourning and no becoming impure for each other. If so, the widow in רבי יוסי's words must be a fully married widow, and רבא's reading falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman whose husband died while they were only engaged
A mourner in the first stage, right after a close relative dies
Becomes ritually impure (a כהן may do so only for close relatives)
The marriage contract payment owed to the wife

steps.whatToRemember: Engaged partners do not mourn each other. That makes it hard to say רבי יוסי's widow exception is about an engaged widow, which puts רבא's rewording under attack.

phrases.english: But a widow from engagement,
does she have mourning?
But didn't Rabbi Chiyya bar Ami teach:
If his engaged wife died,
he is not a mourner for her, and he does not become impure for her.
phrases.notes: The impurity part is about a כהן. He may become impure only for close relatives, and an engaged wife does not count.

phrases.english: And likewise, she,
is not a mourner for him and does not become impure for him.
If she dies, he does not inherit from her.
If he dies, she collects her marriage contract payment!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַלְמָנָה מִן הָאֵירוּסִין מִי אִית לַהּ אִיבּוּל? וְהָתָנֵי
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the widow in רבי יוסי's words is an engaged widow with thirty days of mourning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא בר אמי's ברייתא shows that engaged partners do not mourn each other, so an engaged widow has no mourning period to wait out.
steps.whyThisMatters: If the widow must be a fully married widow, then רבי יוסי's words are about married women. That undoes the whole effort to reread him as talking about engaged women.

steps.title: The question is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier challenge by saying that whether engagement is allowed before תשעה באב is a מחלוקת תנאים, and רבי יוסי follows the stricter view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the earlier קל וחומר challenge against רבי יוסי. It says not everyone agrees that engagement is allowed in the time before תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed it is clearly allowed to get engaged during the mourning before תשעה באב. If some תנאים forbid it, the קל וחומר falls apart, because רבי יוסי can simply follow them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים, the Sages of the משנה era
Rather; drops the earlier approach and brings a new one

phrases.english: Rather, it is a dispute between תנאים.
phrases.notes: He means the question of engaging before תשעה באב. Some תנאים allow it and some forbid it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier קל וחומר challenge to רבי יוסי by denying that its starting assumption is agreed by all.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making it a מחלוקת: רבי יוסי follows the תנא who forbids engagement during communal mourning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees engagement is allowed in the mourning period before תשעה באב, so it should surely be allowed for a widow.
steps.terutzMaskana: Some תנאים forbid engagement before תשעה באב, so רבי יוסי can forbid it for a widow too.

steps.title: A ברייתא that forbids engagement from ראש חודש אב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists what people cut back on from ראש חודש אב, including getting engaged, and adds rules for the week of תשעה באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: From ראש חודש until the fast, people cut back on their activities: business, building and planting, and getting engaged and married. In the week of תשעה באב it is forbidden to cut hair and wash clothes (and to get engaged). Some say: the whole month is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove there is a תנא who forbids engagement before the week of תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists 'getting engaged' among the things people hold back from starting on ראש חודש אב. That is earlier than the week of תשעה באב, so this תנא forbids exactly what the קל וחומר assumed was allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: To cut hair and to wash clothes

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
From ראש חודש until the fast,
phrases.notes: This means ראש חודש אב up to the fast of תשעה באב.

phrases.english: the people cut back on their activities:
from business dealings,
from building and planting,
and from getting engaged and getting married.
In the week in which תשעה באב falls,
it is forbidden to cut hair and to wash clothes
(and it is forbidden to get engaged).
phrases.notes: Some versions have these words in round brackets and some leave them out.

phrases.english: And some say: the whole month is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that backs up the claim of a מחלוקת תנאים in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That a תנא forbids engagement during the communal mourning before the week of תשעה באב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing 'מִלֵּיאָרֵס' among the things restricted from ראש חודש אב.

steps.title: Maybe the ברייתא only forbids the engagement party
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks how we know the ברייתא forbids the engagement itself. Maybe it only forbids making an engagement feast.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objects: How do we know that 'getting engaged' means actually getting engaged? Maybe only making an engagement feast is forbidden, but getting engaged itself is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the proof from the ברייתא. He suggests a different reading of the word 'getting engaged'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא only bans the celebration meal, then it agrees that the engagement itself is allowed. In that case it is no proof that any תנא forbids engagement, and the answer in step 11 loses its support.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine; it is permitted

phrases.english: רב אשי strongly objects to this:
From where do we know that 'to get engaged' means actually getting engaged?
Perhaps it is making an engagement feast
that is forbidden,
but getting engaged itself is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 12's ברייתא is being read.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from the ברייתא that a תנא forbids engagement before תשעה באב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'לֵיאָרֵס' can mean only the engagement feast, so the ברייתא may allow the engagement itself and prove nothing.

steps.title: Then marriage would also mean only the feast
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רב אשי: by his logic, 'marrying' in the ברייתא would also mean only the wedding feast, and marrying itself would be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then 'marrying' too would mean that only making a wedding feast is forbidden, but marrying itself is fine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רב אשי's reading by applying it to the next word in the ברייתא, 'marrying'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists engagement and marriage side by side. If 'engagement' means only its feast, the same should be true of 'marriage'. But it sounds wrong to say marrying itself is allowed during this mourning time.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; testing an idea by its results

phrases.english: If so, then 'from marrying' as well:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out. Both words mean 'to marry'.

phrases.english: it is making a wedding feast that is forbidden,
but marrying itself is fine?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's reading in step 13 by showing what it would mean for the word 'marrying'.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's suggestion that 'לֵיאָרֵס' means only the engagement feast.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reading would make 'לִישָּׂא' mean only the wedding feast, which would allow marrying itself. That is hard to accept.

steps.title: Marriage brings joy even without a feast, engagement does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. A marriage is joyful even without a feast, so marriage itself is forbidden. A plain engagement without a feast has no real joy, so only its feast is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a fair comparison?! Marriage without a feast still has joy. But engagement without a feast, is there any joy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אשי's reading. It shows that engagement and marriage are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mourning rules aim to hold back joy. Marriage itself is joyful, so the ברייתא must forbid the marriage itself. A bare engagement has no joy without the party, so in its case only the feast is forbidden. So רב אשי's reading stands, and the ברייתא still does not prove that engagement itself is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a fair comparison?! The cases are not alike
It makes sense for this one, but not for the other

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not answer the original question. It protects רב אשי's objection. That is why the next step drops the 'מחלוקת תנאים' answer and gives a new one.

phrases.english: How can you compare them?!

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא נִשּׂוּאִין בְּלֹא סְעוּדָה — אִיכָּא שִׂמְחָה,
phrases.english: It makes sense that marriage, even without a feast, has joy,
but engagement without a feast,
is there any joy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14's challenge and so supports רב אשי's objection in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between engagement and marriage in step 14.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Marriage has joy even without a feast, but engagement does not, so the two words in the ברייתא need not be read the same way.

steps.title: Fresh personal mourning is stricter than old communal mourning
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a new answer to the קל וחומר: a widow's new, private mourning is different from the old, public mourning of תשעה באב, so the rules cannot be compared.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: New mourning is different from old mourning, and public mourning is different from the mourning of one person.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the 'מחלוקת תנאים' answer fell apart, רב אשי gives a new answer to the original challenge against רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mourning before תשעה באב is for something long ago (old) and is shared by everyone (public), so it is lighter. A widow mourns a loss that just happened (new) and that is hers alone (private), so it is heavier. Because of these differences, being allowed to get engaged before תשעה באב tells us nothing about a widow, and the קל וחומר is broken.

keyTerms.meaning: New mourning, for a loss that just happened
Old mourning, for something long ago such as the חורבן

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי can forbid a widow to get engaged during her mourning even if engagement is allowed before תשעה באב. Her mourning is new and personal, while the mourning for the חורבן is old and shared by everyone, so it is lighter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general idea: personal mourning for a recent loss is treated more strictly than the national mourning of תשעה באב.

phrases.english: Rather, רב אשי said:
New mourning is different
from old mourning,
phrases.notes: He means the mourning for the חורבן before תשעה באב.

phrases.english: and the mourning of the public is different
from the mourning of one person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer of steps 11–12, which was weakened by steps 13–15, with a new answer to the original challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the cases are different, which breaks the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If engagement is allowed during the mourning before תשעה באב, it should surely be allowed for a widow.
steps.terutzMaskana: A widow's mourning is new and personal, so it is stricter than the old, public mourning of תשעה באב. רבי יוסי can forbid her to get engaged.

steps.title: One brother may do יבום with all the widows
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if some of four married brothers died without children, the eldest surviving brother may do יבום with all of their widows.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: Four brothers were married to four women, and some of the brothers died without children. If the eldest of the surviving brothers wants to do יבום with all of the widows, he is allowed to.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that one brother is allowed to do יבום with several widows at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each widow is bound to the surviving brothers through יבום. The משנה says the eldest brother does not have to share them out. He may take every one of them, and the choice is his (הָרְשׁוּת בְּיָדוֹ).

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. Marks the start of a new משנה.
Levirate marriage: a brother marries his brother's childless widow.
He has permission. The choice is up to him.

steps.confusionAlert: The brothers did not all die. Some died without children, and the eldest is still alive. That is why he can do יבום with their widows.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Four brothers were married to four women
and they died,
phrases.notes: Not all of them died. Some brothers died without children, and the eldest is still alive.

phrases.english: if the eldest among them wants
to do yibum with all of them
he has permission.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אַרְבָּעָה אַחִין נְשׂוּאִין אַרְבַּע נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the mourning discussion of steps 12 to 16 ended. It is not connected to that argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The eldest surviving brother may do יבום with all of his brothers' childless widows.

steps.title: יבום or חליצה with one wife frees the other
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that when a man with two wives dies childless, יבום or חליצה with either one of them releases her צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man was married to two women and died without children, then if either one of them does יבום or חליצה, that releases the other wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second rule. Only one of a dead man's wives needs יבום or חליצה, and that frees the other wife too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The widows of one man count as one unit for יבום. Once one wife has done יבום or חליצה, the brother's duty to that dead brother is complete. The other wife, the צרה, is then free without doing anything herself.

keyTerms.meaning: Marital relations. Here it means the act that completes יבום.
The ceremony that releases a widow from יבום without marriage.
Co-wife: another wife of the same husband.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think each wife needs her own יבום or חליצה. One act, with either wife, frees both of them.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two rules. One brother may do יבום with many widows of different brothers. For the widows of one brother, one יבום or חליצה with either wife takes care of all of them.

phrases.english: One who was married to two women
and died,
the yibum or the chalitza
of one of them
releases her co-wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁהָיָה נָשׂוּי לִשְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים וּמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the second rule in the same משנה. It moves from many brothers' widows to two widows of one brother.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a man dies childless and leaves two wives, יבום or חליצה with either one releases the other wife.
